speaker: Unknown
en: Buyers still want to talk to a person.
zh: 买家仍然想和真人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to buy from an agent, a like, you know, Jack Altman avatar that shows up to a call that is like not really Jack.
zh: 他们不想从一个智能体那里购买，比如说，你知道的，一个像 Jack Altman 的化身出现在电话里，但其实并不是真正的 Jack。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's no higher ROI on my time than spending time with customers.
zh: 所以，把时间花在客户身上，是我时间上回报率最高的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam, what a delight to be here.
zh: Sam，很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited to do this with you.
zh: 我真的很兴奋能和你一起做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome to be here.
zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a fan of this for a really long time, so it's cool to be in this chair.
zh: 我已经是这个节目的粉丝很久了，所以能坐在这个椅子上很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to try to live up to the hype of that.
zh: 我会努力不辜负那样的赞誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually first learned about you by reading Jason Lemkin's Sastra blog back when I was, you know, starting last, trying to learn about sales.
zh: 所以我其实最早是通过读 Jason Lemkin 的 Sastra 博客认识你的，那时候我刚起步，正在学习销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember in there, it was like, you know, Jason's talking about my best, you know, sales rep at EchoSign and he did all of this.
zh: 我记得在里面，你知道的，Jason 在讲我在 EchoSign 最好的销售代表，他做了所有这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I obviously knew about you through Parker, who we both know from, you know, Zenefits and Rippling.
zh: 然后我显然是通过 Parker 认识你的，我们都知道的那位，你知道的，来自 Zenefits 和 Rippling。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've known about you for a long time.
zh: 所以我认识你已经很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, I've gotten to know you well over the last couple of years, but I actually want to start by talking about sort of your sales journey.
zh: 显然，过去几年里我和你熟络起来，但我其实想从谈谈你的销售历程开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So can you talk through like maybe just like a quick summary of like how you came up through sales, you know, a bit about these companies and maybe some of the things that you learned in each of those chapters?
zh: 你能讲一下，比如简单地总结一下，你是如何在销售这行成长起来的，你知道的，关于这些公司的一些情况，以及你在每个阶段学到的一些东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk about lucking into some incredible company.
zh: 我们来聊聊运气好撞进了一些了不起的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Jason and Parker, both of which you alluded to, two of just like the greatest people, but also most influential people on the career that I've had and just like amazing advocates and close friends and all that stuff.
zh: Jason 和 Parker，你刚才都提到了，两位都是最了不起的人，也是对我职业生涯最有影响力的人，同时也是很棒的拥护者和亲密的朋友等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So shout out to those guys.
zh: 所以向他们两位致敬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's see, I grew up in Kansas City and went to University of Missouri when I graduated.
zh: 那么，我在堪萨斯城长大，毕业于密苏里大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was really fortunate that my older brother, Brian, was in San Francisco doing tech sales.
zh: 我非常幸运，我哥哥 Brian 当时在旧金山做科技销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I ever would have ended up out here but for that.
zh: 如果不是因为这个，我觉得我根本不会来到这边。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then 22, moved to San Francisco, got into tech sales.
zh: 于是 22 岁那年，我搬到旧金山，进入了科技销售行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was at EchoSign and I appropriately said like sort of lucked into the relationship with Jason.
zh: 我当时在 EchoSign，很恰当地说，算是运气好结识了 Jason。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just like, you know, using a recruiter that was introducing me to early stage startups.
zh: 我就是，你知道的，用一个把我介绍给早期创业公司的猎头。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them was EchoSign and I had a job offer and I took the job.
zh: 其中一家是 EchoSign，我拿到了工作 offer，就接下了这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started as an SDR, as many folks do in sort of early sales go to market in tech startups.
zh: 于是我从 SDR 做起，很多在科技创业公司早期销售、进入市场阶段的人都经历过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was there for something like six years.
zh: 我在那里待了大概六年。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company did relatively well and afforded me the opportunity to move up into, you know, more senior sales roles within the organization.
zh: 公司做得相对不错，给了我机会在公司内部晋升到更高级的销售职位。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jason introduced me to Parker, went to Zenefits.
zh: Jason 把我介绍给了 Parker，我去了 Zenefits。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was VP of sales there for a few years.
zh: 我在那里做了几年销售副总裁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Crazy years there, which we can get into, but like, I mean, what a growth trajectory that was.
zh: 在那里度过了疯狂的几年，我们可以细聊，但我是说，那是一条多么惊人的增长轨迹啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was awesome.
zh: 是啊，那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I was there for a little under two and a half years.
zh: 你知道，我在那里待了不到两年半。

speaker: Unknown
en: For two of those almost two and a half years, it was incredible.
zh: 其中将近两年半的时间里，那都是难以置信的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then like towards the end, like sort of left turn into lots of lessons and we can, you know, it goes deeper or is not as you want there.
zh: 然后到了后期，就像突然转向，充满了各种教训，我们可以深入聊，或者按你想的来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then prior to doing Founders Fund and ultimately Monaco, most recently in the sort of sales career, I was CRO at Brex.
zh: 然后在去 Founders Fund 以及最终去 Monaco（最近的销售职业经历）之前，我在 Brex 担任 CRO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, same idea, just joined a company that was really exceptional from a very early stage.
zh: 同样的思路，又是加入了一家从很早期就非常出色的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think three times have benefited from the experience of joining when companies are relatively unknown and near zero dollars of revenue and then being able to leave when they were much, much larger and lots of revenue.
zh: 所以我认为有三次，我都受益于这样的经历：在公司还相对不知名、收入接近零美元的时候加入，然后能在我离开时，公司已经大了非常多、收入也非常多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we can spend the least time on this because it's reaching far back into the past, but what did you take away from EchoSign?
zh: 是的，这件事我们可以少花点时间，因为它要回溯到很久以前，但你从 EchoSign 带走了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, those were formative years for you as you thought about what good sales looks like and what a good go-to-market machine looks like, but that's probably where you got a lot of your early ideas about how this stuff should work.
zh: 显然，那些对你来说是塑造性的岁月，当你思考好的销售是什么样子、好的进入市场机器是什么样子的时候，那大概就是你形成了很多关于这套东西应该如何运转的早期想法的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What were your takeaways there?
zh: 你在那里有什么收获？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think there was some- Were you guys up against DocuSign?
zh: 嗯，我觉得有一些—— 你们当时是不是在和 DocuSign 竞争？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's right.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So DocuSign was a competitor.
zh: 所以 DocuSign 是竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: EchoSign was private for like three or four of the years that I was there.
zh: EchoSign 在我在那里的那几年里有三四年是私有公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Adobe had acquired us.
zh: 然后 Adobe 收购了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: EchoSign became AdobeSign after the acquisition.
zh: EchoSign 在被收购后变成了 AdobeSign。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were actually beating DocuSign when Adobe acquired us.
zh: 实际上在 Adobe 收购我们的时候，我们正在打败 DocuSign。

speaker: Unknown
en: And DocuSign is maybe the more familiar name now because EchoSign evolved into AdobeSign.
zh: 而 DocuSign 现在可能是大家更熟悉的名字,因为 EchoSign 后来演变成了 AdobeSign。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's see, a couple of things stand out.
zh: 那么,有几点很突出。

speaker: Unknown
en: First and foremost, and again, I genuinely lucked into this.
zh: 首先,也是最重要的,再说一次,我真的算是运气好碰上了这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's like nothing more influential early in one's sales career than the company that you join.
zh: 我觉得在一个人销售生涯的早期,几乎没有什么比你加入的那家公司更有影响力了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you control a little bit of the success of that business.
zh: 而你对那家业务的成败只有一点点控制权。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I was an SDR and then I was a sales rep and I was one of, let's call it like 10 growing into 40 salespeople.
zh: 你知道,我当时是一名 SDR,后来成了一名销售代表,我是——这么说吧——从 10 个人左右发展到 40 人的销售团队中的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's only so much that I can sort of attribute EchoSign's overall success to me.
zh: EchoSign 的整体成功,我能归功于自己的部分也就那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's funny.
zh: 很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I put this in the...
zh: 我把这个放进了……

speaker: Unknown
en: True but hard to convince people of bucket of things where it's like with, you know, somebody early in their career, it's like, you know, you've got like compensation, title, and quality of company.
zh: 「真实但很难说服别人」的那一类事情里,就是对于一个职业早期的人,你有薪酬、头衔和公司质量这几样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is very hard sometimes to convince people that quality of company is more important than those other things.
zh: 而有时候很难说服别人,公司质量比其他那些东西更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's arguably like, we can of course deal with the others.
zh: 可以说,其他的东西我们当然都能应付。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's arguably like the only thing that matters.
zh: 可以说,公司质量几乎是唯一重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially if you are joining as it is starting to take off.
zh: 尤其是当你正好在它开始起飞的时候加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that I think about these things, a lot of it is like the risk reward.
zh: 我思考这些事情的方式,很大程度上是关于风险回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like the earlier you join almost definitionally, there is more risk.
zh: 而且几乎从定义上说,你加入得越早,风险就越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you can join like right at an inflection point when there is some signal that this company is really about to take off, but you also join in a very early stage where you are like the first, the second, the third, the fourth hire in the role or function that you are joining in.
zh: 但如果你能在恰好的拐点加入——当时已有一些信号表明这家公司真的即将腾飞——同时你又是在非常早期的阶段加入,是你在所加入的职位或职能里的第一个、第二个、第三个、第四个员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the path dependency on the career from there just is like so, so strong.
zh: 那么从那以后,这条职业路径的依赖性就非常、非常强。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So EchoSign, there was this thing that was largely outside of my control that was like the overall success of the business that influenced my personal success as much as anything.
zh: 所以 EchoSign,有一个很大程度上不在我控制范围内的事情,就是整个业务的成功,它对我的个人成功的影响不亚于任何其他因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is like a different variable here.
zh: 我觉得这里还有另一个变量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I sort of lucked into or found a career path that is a good fit for me.
zh: 我算是运气好,或者说是找到了一条很适合我的职业道路。

speaker: Unknown
en: I enjoy this a lot and I'm pretty good at it in ways that had I tried something different, I would have probably been less good and enjoyed it less.
zh: 我非常享受这份工作,而且我相当擅长,换作如果我尝试了别的方向,我可能会没那么擅长,也不会那么享受。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to go to Zenefits.
zh: 我想聊聊 Zenefits。

speaker: Unknown
en: Parker, obviously one of the great founders of the last decade.
zh: Parker 显然是过去十年最出色的创始人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, obviously, Zenefits in some ways, like, you know, he basically rebuilt Zenefits and figured out, like, you know, these are the product things that need to happen for this to be a super durable company.
zh: 而且你知道,显然,Zenefits 在某种程度上,你知道,他基本上重建了 Zenefits,并想清楚了,你知道,要让这家公司成为一个超级持久的企业,需要在产品上做哪些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was really strong product market fit there.
zh: 但当时确实有非常强的产品市场契合度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think equally notable, the go to market machine and apparatus that early Zenefits had was like remarkable.
zh: 但我认为同样值得注意的是,早期 Zenefits 拥有的 go-to-market 机器和体系非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like, yes, in the end, like some product things weren't there.
zh: 所以,是的,最终,某些产品上的东西是缺失的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, can you talk about that early scaling?
zh: 但是,你能谈谈那段早期的规模化扩张吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think it was like.
zh: 因为我觉得大概是……

speaker: Unknown
en: At least of that, you know, it was maybe what, 2013, 14 that it was scaling, something like that?
zh: 至少,你知道,大概是 2013 年、14 年在扩张,差不多那个时候?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I joined in December of 2013 and then Parker and I both left around the same day, left in quotes, around the same day in 2016.
zh: 是的,我在 2013 年 12 月加入,然后 Parker 和我几乎在同一天离开——带引号的「离开」——在 2016 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was February of 2016.
zh: 我记得是 2016 年 2 月。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk about what building that go-to-market machine looked like in those early days?
zh: 你能谈谈在那些早期日子里,搭建那台 go-to-market 机器是什么样子的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's see.
zh: 那么,让我想想。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've talked about Parker a little bit.
zh: 我们已经聊了一点 Parker。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think an inspiration in a couple of ways, just in terms of like learning so much on how he is a founder and CEO and runs a business.
zh: 我觉得他在几个方面都是一种启发,就比如说从他作为一名创始人兼 CEO 如何经营一门生意上,我学到了非常多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just like a lot of lessons there that you sort of organically learn from.
zh: 那里面有很多经验教训,你是自然而然地从中学习到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's one that you like come back to a lot?
zh: 有哪一条是你经常回想起来的?

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a thought exercise in March of 2014 that we, when I signed up for Zenefits, we had a revenue target of going from effectively zero, maybe it was a few hundred K when I joined in December of 2013.
zh: 2014 年 3 月有一个思维练习,当我加入 Zenefits 的时候,我们有一个营收目标:从实际上为零——可能我 2013 年 12 月加入时是几十万 K——

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were creating our 2014 plan.
zh: 所以当时我们正在制定 2014 年的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to go from effectively zero to $10 million of ARR by the end of 2014.
zh: 我们想在 2014 年底之前,从实际上为零做到 1000 万美元的 ARR。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in 12 months.
zh: 也就是在 12 个月之内。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which by the way, in 2014, now that people are like, ah, but that's like, that's like today, somebody saying zero to a hundred.
zh: 顺便说一句,在 2014 年——现在人们会说,啊,那算什么——那就像今天某人说从零到一个亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was sort of unheard of.
zh: 那在当时几乎是闻所未闻的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Parker, let's see, Parker, as he should, has sort of like very ambitious, dream big aspirations and expectations.
zh: 而 Parker,让我想想,Parker,正如他应该的那样,有着非常雄心勃勃、敢于做梦的抱负和期望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so zero to 10 million was like, there weren't a lot of other startups that were doing it.
zh: 所以从零到 1000 万,当时并没有多少其他创业公司能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then early in the year of 2014, we were trending towards more than that.
zh: 然后 2014 年初,我们的增长趋势已经超过了那个数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so he sat me and Matt Epstein down, who was leading marketing, and said, let's go through a thought exercise of instead of finishing the year at 10 million ARR, which is our like, you know, stretch goal or however you want to frame it, what does it look like if we finish at 20?
zh: 于是他让我和当时负责市场营销的 Matt Epstein 坐下来，说，我们来做一个思维实验，与其以 1000 万 ARR 结束这一年——这是我们的，你知道的，冲刺目标或者随你怎么定义——如果我们以 2000 万结束，那会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to back into sort of like...
zh: 然后我们想倒推出类似……

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the headcount implications of doing this?
zh: 这样做对人员编制有什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the sort of like lead implications of doing this?
zh: 这样做对线索数量有什么影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: How many leads would we need?
zh: 我们需要多少线索？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would the marketing spend look like?
zh: 市场营销支出会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you sort of like do whiteboard session on, I don't know, Monday night or whatever, and you end at 1 a.m. And we kind of like look around the room and Parker's like, well, we're not going to tell the board yet, but we're going to do this.
zh: 然后你就在，比如周一晚上之类的某个晚上，开一场白板会议，一直开到凌晨一点。我们互相看了看，Parker 说，好吧，我们还不会告诉董事会，但我们就这么干了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And three days later, he told the board like the new goal is $20 million.
zh: 三天后，他告诉董事会，新目标是 2000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a takeaway that you can apply that process to all sorts of aspects of the business.
zh: 所以这里有一个可以借鉴的点，你可以把这个流程应用到业务的方方面面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And is that basically, does that boil down to just like people rise to the level of expectations you set and just pushing the boundaries of what great could be just sparks more achievement?
zh: 这基本上是不是就是说，人们会达到你所设定期望的水平，只要不断突破「优秀」的边界，就能激发更多的成就？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that kind of it?
zh: 是这个意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's something there.
zh: 我觉得确实有这个因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think that there's something around manufacturing urgency and having really audacious goals.
zh: 我也认为这和制造紧迫感、设定真正大胆的目标有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's probably several takeaways, but that specific process is one that I try and apply.
zh: 可能有好几个可以借鉴的点，但这个具体的流程是我一直在努力应用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can be something like a revenue target.
zh: 它可以是像营收目标这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can also be something like, how long is something going to take?
zh: 也可以是像「这件事要花多长时间？」这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would it take actually if we needed to do this in a shorter amount of time?
zh: 如果我们需要在更短的时间内完成这件事，实际上需要付出什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what would sort of be the trade-offs in those sorts of things?
zh: 以及这些事情里的权衡取舍会是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's just operating rhythm of the business, something like that.
zh: 所以这只是业务的运营节奏之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have these ambitious goals for the year.
zh: 那么你为这一年设定了这些雄心勃勃的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then like what goes into that?
zh: 那么具体需要做什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when you said, okay, what does need to be true to go to 20 instead of 10?
zh: 比如你说，好，要达到 2000 万而不是 1000 万，需要满足什么条件？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what's the, what is that conversation?
zh: 那是一个什么样的对话？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think one of the things that we benefited from quite strong product market fit at Zenefits.
zh: 嗯，我觉得我们在 Zenefits 受益于相当强的产品市场契合度。

zh: 今天，尤其是如果你在做 B2B，买家仍然想和一个真人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to buy from an agent, a like, you know, Jack Altman avatar that shows up to a call that is like not really Jack.
zh: 他们不想从一个智能体、从一个你知道的、出现在电话里却不是真 Jack 的 Jack Altman 化身那里购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: So
zh: 所以

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no higher ROI on my time, maybe on, I would suspect, our customers' time, than spending time with customers.
zh: 我的时间没有比花在客户身上更高的 ROI 了，我猜，我们客户的时间也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the things that we're able to leverage with AI allow us to spend far more of our time, whether you're a founder or a salesperson, on that human connection, developing relationships, customer facing.
zh: 而我们能够借助 AI 杠杆化的很多东西，让我们无论你是创始人还是销售，都能把多得多的时间花在那种人际连接、发展关系、面对客户上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second thing is this category of creative, operationally complex campaigns.
zh: 我认为第二件事是这一类有创意、运营上复杂的营销活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've talked about a bunch of them.
zh: 我们已经谈过很多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could do like a ChatGPT conversation where you're like, can you come up with some marketing ideas for me?
zh: 你可以做一个 ChatGPT 对话，问它：你能帮我想一些营销点子吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it would be hard for that to result in the plane, as an example.
zh: 我觉得这很难产出那架飞机那样的东西，作为一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that today AI will sort of pattern match to things that have already been done because that is what AI is trained on.
zh: 我认为今天 AI 会某种程度上模式匹配到已经被做过的事情，因为那就是 AI 被训练的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you are trying to do something like truly creative, innovative, innovative,
zh: 所以如果你想做真正有创意、创新的事情，

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is more likely to surface inside the four walls of your company by doing the sort of like ideation that I talked about, which is let's come up with two ideas each person, multiply by four, that's eight ideas, put them on a whiteboard, talk through each of them, pick the two or three of the best ones that we're going to do.
zh: 我认为它更可能出现在你公司的四面墙之内，通过我做过的那种构思：我们每个人想两个点子，乘以四，那就是八个点子，把它们放到白板上，逐个讨论，挑出我们要做的两三个最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Monaco and AI actually give us the ability to spend our time doing those things.
zh: Monaco 和 AI 实际上给了我们能力去把时间花在那些事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is how I spend my time with customers.
zh: 那就是我和客户度过时间的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Less about the sort of like, how should you be meeting with customers?
zh: 少谈一点那种，比如：你应该怎么和客户会面？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do like, how should you sell?
zh: 我喜欢谈：你应该怎么销售？

speaker: Unknown
en: Those sorts of things.
zh: 那类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's coming up with like creative campaign ideas.
zh: 但那是想出有创意的营销活动点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Count me in as like one of the people that comes up with the ideas that we put on the whiteboard.
zh: 把我算作那种想出点子放到白板上的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's awesome.
zh: 对，那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I guess like on that last piece, is there anything worth talking about in terms of like how to actually sell or like the practice of, you know, the time with the customers itself?
zh: 然后我猜在那最后一点上，关于实际怎么销售、以及你说的与客户相处的时间本身的实践，有什么值得谈的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are two things that stand out as, and then there's like a laundry list below it, right?
zh: 我觉得有两件事是突出的，然后下面还有一长串清单，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is maybe the like broader generic advice that I would have to certainly founders that are starting to sell their product and don't have a lot of go-to-market experience that I think have maybe more impact than any other, you know, below these two.
zh: 但这也许是我会给那些开始销售自己产品、却没有太多走向市场经验的创始人——我认为比下面这两点之外的任何建议都更有影响——的更宽泛的通用建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is I would be fairly prescriptive about how to effectively buy your product.
zh: 第一点，我会对如何有效地购买你的产品相当有指导性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you aren't educating the buyer on how to onboard, receive value, and ultimately buy your product, the customer doesn't know how to buy your product.
zh: 因为如果你不在如何上手、获得价值、并最终购买你的产品上教育买家，客户不知道怎么购买你的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would come in with a bit of a combination of agenda and opinion.
zh: 所以我会带着一点议程加观点的组合走进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: On here is the happy path.
zh: 内容是：这是理想路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: From where we sit today, and if this resonates with you and is something that you think you can receive value around, to like where we are when you are fully onboarded and receiving value from the product, and we can just sort of roadmap together.
zh: 从我们今天所处的位置——如果这与你产生共鸣、是你认为你能从中获得价值的东西——到你完全上手并从产品中获得价值时的状态，我们可以一起做个路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here are the different steps.
zh: 这里是不同的步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, like Mr.
zh: 现在，比如先生——

speaker: Unknown
en: Customer, is there anything that I have left out of this process that is important to you that we should incorporate?
zh: 客户，这个流程里有没有什么我遗漏的、对你们很重要的东西需要纳入进来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's like security checks that you may need to go through or procurement that we want to introduce or legal review that I haven't included.
zh: 比如你们可能需要走的安全审查，或者我们想引入的采购流程，或者我还没包括进去的法务审核。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we sort of start with, and this is very abstract, we sort of start with like we, you know, meeting two, we come with like our pre-built custom environment to show you exactly what it would look like on our product.
zh: 但我们大致是这样开始的，这很抽象，我们大致是这样开始的，比如，你知道，第二次会议，我们会带上我们预先构建好的定制环境，向你确切展示在我们的产品上它会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that resonates with you, we put you in like a two-week free trial of the product.
zh: 如果这让你产生共鸣，我们就给你安排一个大概两周的产品免费试用。

speaker: Unknown
en: During that trial, like here are the outcomes that we're going to be driving towards.
zh: 在试用期间，比如，这些是我们将要努力实现的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we deliver on these outcomes, we like onboard the rest of the team.
zh: 如果我们交付了这些目标，我们就比如把团队的其他成员也 onboarding 进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's like schedule meetings that sort of align to these different steps.
zh: 我们来安排与这些不同步骤相对应的会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then you and the customer aren't flying blind.
zh: 这样你和客户就不会盲飞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the thing that happens more often than anything when I meet with founders, it's sort of like we have so many of these opportunities that are in like purgatory.
zh: 我见创始人时遇到最多的情况，就是我们有太多这样的机会卡在像炼狱一样的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it's like, we pitched them.
zh: 就是那种，我们给他们做了 pitch。

speaker: Unknown
en: They said they liked it.
zh: 他们说他们喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ended the call.
zh: 我们结束了通话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've followed up three times.
zh: 我已经跟进三次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They aren't really responding.
zh: 他们基本不回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they do respond, it's like, give me a week and I'll get back to you.
zh: 即使他们回复了，也是那种，给我一周时间，我会回复你。

speaker: Unknown
en: A week passes, they don't get back to me.
zh: 一周过去了，他们没有回复我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's because we haven't aligned on the happy path to receiving value from the product that we're selling.
zh: 而这是因为我们没有就从我们销售的产品中获得价值的理想路径达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll pause there.
zh: 所以我先在这里停一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like one of the two things.
zh: 这是两件事中的一件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the other?
zh: 另一件是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is like a little bit of an urgency driver where if you can create some form of FOMO, for lack of a better word, I think that much of sales is psychology.
zh: 第二件事算是一个 urgency 的驱动因素，如果你能制造某种形式的 FOMO,找不到更好的词的话，我认为销售的很大一部分是心理学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for many customers, what I'm about to articulate is true.
zh: 所以对很多客户来说，我接下来要阐述的是真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We certainly never want to say anything that is untrue or misleading.
zh: 我们当然绝不想说任何不真实或误导性的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we have, you know, we're in the month of July.
zh: 但是如果我们，你知道，现在是七月份。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we have a goal to onboard three customers to pilots in the month of July, what we articulate to a customer as part of the maybe like first call when we are receiving feedback, like, yeah, this is actually really cool.
zh: 如果我们的目标是在七月份让三个客户加入 pilot,那么当我们在大概第一次通话中收到反馈时，比如，对，这确实很酷，我们对客户阐述的是这样的内容：我很想试试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to try it.
zh: 我们说的是类似这样的：这个月我们会让三个客户加入我们的 pilot 项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we say is something like, we are onboarding three customers into our pilot program this month.
zh: 那三个名额里有两个已经有主了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two of those spots are already spoken for.
zh: —(照编号对应)

speaker: Unknown
en: There is much interest in the third spot.
zh: 第三个名额有很多兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you would like to move forward with a pilot, if you could let me know, that would be like really appreciated on my end.
zh: 如果你想推进 pilot,如果你能告诉我，那我这边会非常感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also like, I can't guarantee the spot if you don't speak for it today.
zh: 但同样，比如，如果你今天不把这个名额占下来，我不能保证这个名额还留着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's true because you can only onboard so many at this stage.
zh: 而且我认为这是真实的，因为在这个阶段你只能 onboarding 这么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it does sort of force a decision and potentially drive some urgency.
zh: 但它确实会促成决定，并可能带来一些紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is like a psychological aspect to this where it's like, oh gosh, two, two thirds of the spots are already spoken for.
zh: 这里面有一种心理学层面的东西，就是，哦天哪，三分之二的名额已经有主了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I better speak up.
zh: 比如，我最好赶紧表态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: To like, you know, get this thing that a lot of folks are already incredibly interested in.
zh: 去把很多已经非常感兴趣的人都在争的东西拿到手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I assume also important in all of this is sort of just like having like a willingness to disqualify when you genuinely think that the product is not gonna help the customer.
zh: 我猜想在这其中同样重要的是，当你真心认为产品不会帮到客户时，要有一种愿意取消其资格的态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think people can feel that.
zh: 而且我觉得人们能感受到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you're like, hey, my goal here is not to sell you something that you don't need or want.
zh: 比如，如果你说，嘿，我这里的目标不是卖给你不需要或不想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: My goal is to sell you something that's gonna be useful to you for years.
zh: 我的目标是卖给你一件未来很多年都对你有用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if I don't think that that's gonna be the case, I'm gonna stop selling it to you.
zh: 所以如果我不认为情况会是这样，我就不会再向你推销了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Man, when you say that, it's interesting where my mind goes, which is something different than what you just said.
zh: 天哪，当你说这些的时候，有意思的是我的思绪走向了另一个地方，和你刚才说的不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it is true that growth solves a lot of problems.
zh: 但我认为增长确实能解决很多问题，这是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think an input to that is something like demand solves a lot of problems.
zh: 我认为它的一个输入是，需求能解决很多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you just articulated, I think, is a symptom of not enough demand.
zh: 而你刚才阐述的，我认为，是需求不足的一种症状。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is where founders and salespeople are like hanging on for dear life to the like one guy that I pitched over the last couple of days because like they kind of seemed interested.
zh: 正因如此，创始人和销售才会死死抓住过去几天里 pitch 过的那一个人不放，因为他们好像有点感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're like, I've got like four more calls I should get to.
zh: 但如果你是那种，我还有四个电话要打。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, I think this is going to be painful.
zh: 而且，我觉得这会是很痛苦的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, I get paid also on you retaining.
zh: 顺便说一句，我的报酬也和你留续有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like, I don't think I want to sell this to you anymore.
zh: 所以我不再想把这东西卖给你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can, Parker, I stole this from him.
zh: 你可以，Parker,这是从他那儿偷来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can sort of swipe left.
zh: 你可以往左滑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never been on one of the dating apps, but I think Tinder, you sort of like swipe right if you like them and swipe left if you don't.
zh: 我从来没上过交友软件，但我记得 Tinder 好像是如果你喜欢对方就右滑，不喜欢就左滑。

speaker: Unknown
en: An abundant pipeline allows you to only try to sell the product to people who need it.
zh: 充足的销售管线让你可以只把产品卖给真正需要它的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I say that, it's not disrespectful to the customer or being inefficient about not following up.
zh: 我这么说,并不是对客户不敬,也不是不跟进、效率低下。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually that you are focusing your resources on the people that are truly interested that will receive the most value from the product and not on the person that took a call that was like...
zh: 而是说你把资源聚焦在真正感兴趣、能从产品中获得最大价值的人身上,而不是那个接了个电话然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: Said a lot of niceties, but like actually probably isn't actually interested.
zh: 说了一堆客套话，但实际上可能根本不感兴趣的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, a lot of it is like a not now, but you know, let's come back to this.
zh: 顺便说一句，很多时候是"不是现在，但我们回头再谈"。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, we have so many customers.
zh: 哦，我们有好多客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's somebody who's like, you know, I am just getting started.
zh: 如果有人是那种，你知道，我刚起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really have product market fit yet.
zh: 我还没有产品市场契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have any reps. You know, I'm interested.
zh: 我还没有任何销售代表。你知道，我挺感兴趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might be like, sure, if you want to buy it now, but like it might be better if you bought this in six months once you're going a little bit.
zh: 你可能会说，行，如果你现在想买也可以，但如果你过六个月等你跑起来一点再买，可能会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're four months in, four or five months in, launched in February.
zh: 我们进行到第四个月了，四五个月，二月上线的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Monaco does an awesome job of continuing to engage with older customers on our behalf.
zh: Monaco 在替我们持续接触老客户方面做得非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I cannot tell you, well, I can tell you.
zh: 但我没法告诉你——好吧,我还是能告诉你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amount of times where I'm just sitting there and resurrected from what effectively is The Dead, a company that we demoed back in February that Monaco sort of re-engages with on my behalf, response comes in, I see the response and it's like, I'm ready to go.
zh: 有太多次我就坐在那儿,然后从" effectively 的死人堆里"复活——我们二月 demo 过的一家公司,Monaco 替我重新接上联系,回复来了,我一看回复,就是那种:我准备好下单了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, all of this stems from more demos in February, right?
zh: 再说一遍，这一切都源于二月做了更多 demo，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think lots of sort of anecdotes of what a demand-rich environment evolves to.
zh: 所以我觉得有很多这样的轶事,展示了一个需求充沛的环境会演变成什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam, this was awesome.
zh: Sam,这期太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learn a bunch every time we talk.
zh: 每次和你聊我都能学到很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for doing this with me.
zh: 谢谢你和我一起做这期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are the best.
zh: 你是最棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for partnering with me on Monaco.
zh: 非常感谢你在 Monaco 上和我合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just an absolute pleasure to come on the show.
zh: 来上这个节目真是绝对的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thanks for having me.
zh: 所以感谢你邀请我。
